newsitem.title: UK: Dollar firms in late Europe ahead of U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firms in late Europe ahead of U.S. holiday.

text.p: The dollar was firmer in late European trade in fairly thin trade, making its gains largely on the back of position squaring ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
A slew of U.S. data had little net impact on the dollar but pressured U.S. bonds, erasing early gains. The dollar also shrugged off an over 30 point fall in the Dow industrials.

"The orders data were a bit strong and while we might see some more short-term (dollar/mark) gains, we tend to see the dollar rally running out of steam soon," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.

U.S. October durable goods orders rose 0.1 percent against an average of analysts' forecasts pointing to a 2.0 percent fall. Ex-defence orders were up 0.4 percent against a 2.2 percent expected fall and a 17.3 percent rise in electronic orders was the highest on record. U.S. third quarter GDP growth was revised down to 2.0 percent from a previous 2.2 percent but was still above expectations of a revision to 1.7 percent growth.
The dollar against the mark was trading at 1.5275/85 at 1623 GMT, just below a late session high of 1.5285 marks. It stood at 1.5242/52 late Tuesday in Europe.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, speaking at a parliamentary debate on monetary union, repeated his thoughts that the dollar was undervalued, which was seen providing some dollar support.
Juppe also said he would ask the G7 to take up the issue of the dollar's weakness. Dealers said this was providing stronger underpinning for the dollar.
Juppe said the mark-French franc parity should not be changed.
Dollar/French franc was trading at 5.1720/50, off a session high of 5.1830 and close to late Tuesday's 5.1717/27.
The Swiss franc was also softer against the dollar, holding around the 1.29 franc level but lacking the impetus to retest Tuesday's 21-month high.
Dollar/Swiss at 1654 GMT stood at 1.2910/20 against 1.2906/16 francs Tuesday.
Dollar/yen remained firm in European trade, pushing above the 113 yen level on the back of a subdued Tankan quarterly survey.
Analysts said the report showed only a modest economic recovery and confirmed expectations that Japanese interest rates will remain stable for the foreseeable future.
The dollar stood at 113.25/35 yen at 1701 GMT after touching a session peak of 113.41 but still above late Tuesday's level of 112.59/69.
Dealers said that while trade was relatively quiet in the dollar markets ahead of the U.S. holiday, sterling continued to provide some post-UK budget excitement.

Sterling/mark cleared resistance at 2.56 marks to set fresh 32-month highs, trading at 2.5615/22 at 1705 GMT. Cable was steady around $1.6750 after slipping below $1.68 in afternoon trade but was still seen as being well-supported.
